digest.lead: Claude Code gets its second patch release this week with v2.1.140, focusing on developer experience improvements and bug fixes for agent workflows.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, the broader AI agent ecosystem is seeing new tooling for analytics and state management, reflecting growing enterprise adoption of agent-based workflows.

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.140 Improves Agent Tools and Fixes Critical Bugs
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code release enhances agent tool matching with case-insensitive subagent types and fixes several critical issues [1]. Key fixes include resolving a `/goal` command hang when hooks are disabled and addressing hot-reload problems with symlinked configuration files [1].
key_points: Agent tool matching now accepts flexible formatting (e.g., 'Code Reviewer' maps to 'code-reviewer')
Fixed `/goal` command hanging silently when hooks are disabled - now shows clear error messages
Resolved configuration hot-reload issues with symlinked settings files
stories.impact: These fixes directly address pain points for developers using Claude Code's agent features in production, particularly teams with complex configuration setups and hook management workflows.

stories.headline: New Analytics and State Management Tools Emerge for AI Agents
stories.summary: Two new developer tools are gaining community attention: Voker, a YC S24 company offering analytics for AI agents, and Statewright, an open-source project for visual state machines designed to make AI agents more reliable [3][4]. Both projects reflect growing interest in production-ready agent tooling.
stories.impact: These tools address critical gaps in AI agent development - observability and reliability - that become essential as teams move from prototypes to production deployments.

Show HN: Statewright – Visual state machines that make AI agents reliable

stories.headline: Use case-insensitive agent type names in Claude Code configurations
stories.summary: Claude Code now accepts agent type names with any casing and separators. This makes configuration more flexible and reduces errors from formatting inconsistencies.
actionable_steps: In your Claude Code configuration, use any casing for agent types (e.g., 'Code Reviewer', 'code-reviewer', 'CODE_REVIEWER')
Test that your existing configurations still work with the new flexible matching
Update documentation to reflect the more flexible naming convention

stories.headline: Configure streaming timeout for better connection handling
stories.summary: The new CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable lets you customize how long Claude Code waits before timing out idle streaming connections. This helps prevent unnecessary disconnections during long-running operations.
actionable_steps: Choose a timeout value in milliseconds (default is 90000 for 90 seconds)
Restart Claude Code for the setting to take effect

stories.headline: Use _meta annotation to prevent large MCP tool results from being truncated
stories.summary: Claude Code now supports preserving large tool results (like database schemas) up to 500K characters by adding a special metadata annotation. This prevents important data from being cut off during processing.
actionable_steps: Add `_meta["anthropic/maxResultSizeChars"]` annotation to your MCP tool result
Set the value to your desired character limit (up to 500,000)
Test with large results like database schemas to verify they pass through completely

stories.headline: Enable Amazon Bedrock support with Mantle integration
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.94 added support for Amazon Bedrock through Mantle integration. This allows you to use Claude Code with Amazon's Bedrock service instead of the default API endpoints, potentially offering better performance or compliance for enterprise users.
actionable_steps: Set the environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE=1 in your system or terminal
Restart Claude Code to apply the new configuration
Verify the connection is working by running a test query

stories.headline: Use `/tui fullscreen` for flicker-free Claude Code rendering
stories.summary: The `/tui fullscreen` command switches Claude Code to a flicker-free rendering mode within the same conversation. This improves visual stability and reduces screen flicker during interactions.
actionable_steps: Press Enter to activate flicker-free rendering mode
